topic: Angle-driven alignment review, wave one, lane wave1-deepseek: angles 1 to 5

focus: Angle 1 — routing artifact parity, system-deep-loop hub

findingDetails.title: Seven hub routing artifacts carry six disagreeing version values, two with no version key
findingDetails.evidence: SKILL.md=3.0.0.0, mode-registry.json=2.0.0.1, hub-router.json=2.0.1.1, ROUTER.md=1.0.1.0, description.json=2.2.3.0, leaf-manifest.json has no version key, graph-metadata.json has no version key. Both sibling hubs keep SKILL.md and description.json in exact parity; sk-code additionally keeps mode-registry.json == hub-router.json.
findingDetails.impact: A reader or drift gate cannot tell whether these artifacts are the same generation.
findingDetails.recommendation: Establish one generation field shared across the hub-root artifacts, or document that they version independently and correct SKILL.md/description.json parity. No fix was made during this review.
findingDetails.scopeProof: Read all seven hub-root artifacts directly plus the same five artifacts in sk-code and cli-external-orchestration as a fleet control.

findingDetails.title: SKILL.md states two improvement-lane counts and a six-mode roster no artifact supports
findingDetails.evidence: SKILL.md:27 and :58 say two lanes; SKILL.md:161 says three lanes; SKILL.md:131 says six registered modes. mode-registry.json holds five modes with no skill-improvement entry, loop-host.cjs:40 validates a two-mode set, README.md:62 says three lanes, mode-registry.json:16 says two, description.json:3 says five modes.
findingDetails.impact: A reader told to extend the six registered modes is pointed at a roster that does not exist, and the lane count is self-contradictory inside one document.
findingDetails.recommendation: Reconcile the two lane counts and the registered-mode count against mode-registry.json. No fix was made during this review.
findingDetails.scopeProof: Counted modes independently in registry, hub-router routerSignals, leaf-manifest mode entries and description.json prose; grepped the improvement packet for a third lane.

findingDetails.title: hub-router.json and ROUTER.md state opposite always-loaded-preamble policies
findingDetails.evidence: hub-router.json:13 sets defaultResource to a two-element array [ROUTER.md, mode-registry.json]. ROUTER.md:67-69 states no always-loaded preamble exists and sets DEFAULT_RESOURCE = []. The compiled-routing authored validator requires a scalar string for a non-null defaultResource; this hub's own registry-compiler branch never reads the field, so no live route fails today.
findingDetails.impact: An operator reading the two artifacts learns two different no-match behaviours; the array shape is outside the authored contract on any hub whose compiler does read the field.
findingDetails.recommendation: Decide the hub's no-match policy once and make both artifacts state it in a shape the compiler accepts. No fix was made during this review.
findingDetails.scopeProof: Read both artifacts at their exact lines, read the compiler validator that constrains the field, and grepped the hub's compiler branch for the field.

findingDetails.title: Identical 61-leaf sets for both improvement lanes against a two-leaf ROUTER.md scope
findingDetails.evidence: Both lane entries carry 61 leaves and the arrays compare byte-equal (JSON.stringify equality true), mixing 15 agent-improvement files into the benchmark lane and 39 benchmark files into the agent lane. generate-leaf-manifest.cjs:161-163 promises distinct independently addressable leaf sets for exactly this N-to-1 fan-out. ROUTER.md:100-103 scopes MODEL_BENCHMARK to two leaves, and SKILL.md:120 requires the two artifacts to stay in sync.
findingDetails.impact: The lanes are not independently addressable, and the manifest disagrees with ROUTER.md by a factor of thirty on the artifact pair a hub rule requires to agree.
findingDetails.recommendation: Scope each lane's manifest entry to its own packet sub-tree and reconcile ROUTER.md with it. No fix was made during this review.
findingDetails.scopeProof: Compared the two lane arrays programmatically for byte equality and counted lane-specific members in each; read the generator contract and the hub sync rule.

findingDetails.title: Retired families still present in hub keyword block and graph-metadata discovery terms
findingDetails.evidence: SKILL.md:8 lists conformance, standard-authority, conformance-review, read-only-default, context-gathering and reuse-catalog; graph-metadata.json:124 carries standard-authority in derived.key_topics and :113 carries skill benchmark in derived.trigger_phrases. No registry mode or alias names any of them.
findingDetails.impact: Derived discovery terms can still surface the hub for a request naming a family the hub no longer routes.
findingDetails.recommendation: Regenerate both surfaces from the live roster. No fix was made during this review.
findingDetails.scopeProof: Tested each residue term against every registry workflowMode and alias; grepped the improvement packet for a reintroducing registry.

findingDetails.title: Two model-benchmark registry aliases are absent from the hub scoring vocabulary
findingDetails.evidence: mode-registry.json:147 declares prompt framework benchmark and benchmark-harness as model-benchmark aliases; hub-router.json:58-60 scopes the model-benchmark-aliases class to /deep:model-benchmark, model benchmark and benchmark a model. Neither registry term appears in any class, and SKILL.md:8 carries benchmark-harness as a hub keyword.
findingDetails.impact: A request phrased with those terms scores no mode and reaches the hub defer outcome.
findingDetails.recommendation: Align the scoring vocabulary with the registry aliases, or remove the aliases. No fix was made during this review.
findingDetails.scopeProof: Computed registry-only and hub-only term sets per mode by set difference rather than sampling, then checked adjacent classes for the missing terms.

results.summary: Angle 1 names seven artifacts and five properties; all seven and all five were covered, but four properties disagree and the spec names no resolution authority.
The phase spec carries no per-iteration checklist rows; its REQ rows are assessed at synthesis.

focus: Angle 2 — routing artifact parity, sk-code and cli-external-orchestration hubs

findingDetails.title: cli-external-orchestration ROUTER.md omits the seventh registered mode cli-hermes in all three roster statements
findingDetails.evidence: ROUTER.md:24-25 lists six modes with no cli-hermes; :38-46 opens the INTENT MODEL and supplies exactly six per-mode bullets (grep -c '^- **cli-' returns 6); :143-144 closes with the same six names; lines 1-70 contain zero hermes mentions. mode-registry.json registers seven including cli-hermes as packetKind workflow, hub-router.json carries seven routerSignals and cli-hermes in tieBreak, leaf-manifest.json carries a nine-leaf cli-hermes entry, SKILL.md:31 carries a cli-hermes mode-table row, and this same ROUTER.md's RESOURCE_MAP carries a HERMES key with two cli-hermes paths.
findingDetails.impact: The document this hub names as its stage-two routing authority routes a mode in its machine block while its human-facing contract states the mode does not exist, so the newest registered mode has no described intent model or leaf set.
findingDetails.recommendation: Add cli-hermes to all three ROUTER.md roster statements and its intent-model bullet. No fix was made during this review.
findingDetails.scopeProof: Counted per-mode intent bullets programmatically, grepped lines 1-70 for hermes, and cross-read registry, hub-router, leaf-manifest, SKILL.md mode table and ROUTER.md's own RESOURCE_MAP.

findingDetails.title: cli-external-orchestration SKILL.md:74 says all six modes against seven in the same file and five other statements
findingDetails.evidence: SKILL.md:74 says ROUTER.md defines the leaf-intent model for all six modes, while SKILL.md:3, :15, :54 and :190 say seven, README.md says seven five times, and description.json:3 enumerates all seven by name. A regex count of mode-count phrases returned seven/four times against six/once.
findingDetails.impact: A reader of the hub's routing prose receives a roster size that contradicts the hub's own registry, mode table and description.
findingDetails.recommendation: Correct the six-to-seven in the ROUTER.md description sentence as part of the F007 fix. No fix was made during this review.
findingDetails.scopeProof: Regular-expression extracted every mode-count phrase in SKILL.md, README.md and ROUTER.md rather than reading for one, then compared against the registry roster.

findingDetails.title: cli-external-orchestration splits the mode-registry/hub-router version pair that sk-code keeps in parity
findingDetails.evidence: cli mode-registry.json=1.2.0.2 vs hub-router.json=1.2.1.2 (differ); sk-code mode-registry.json=4.1.0.1 vs hub-router.json=4.1.0.1 (match). The SKILL.md/description.json pair matches in both hubs (cli 1.5.0.0/1.5.0.0; sk-code 4.2.2.0/4.2.2.0), isolating the divergence to one pair on one hub.
findingDetails.impact: Completes the fleet version matrix begun in iteration 1: system-deep-loop splits both pairs, cli-external-orchestration splits one, and sk-code the reference hub splits neither.
findingDetails.recommendation: Either bring this pair into parity or introduce the single shared generation field F001 proposes. No fix was made during this review.
findingDetails.scopeProof: Read all five version-bearing artifacts in all three hubs as a matrix rather than comparing one pair in isolation.

findingDetails.scopeProof: Compared all seven cli mode leaf sets member by member to find lane-unique references, then searched ROUTER.md prose for a sentence accounting for one.

focus: Angle 3 — SKILL.md against references and assets

findingDetails.title: Leaf-manifest generator skips symlinks, leaving 12 sk-code workflow doctrine files untyped
findingDetails.evidence: Four sk-code surfaces each carry references/workflow-implement.md, workflow-debug.md and workflow-verify.md as symlinks to ../../shared/references/. None of the 12 appears in any leaf-manifest entry, while all 12 resolve on disk. Every unreachable file in the fleet is a symlink (12 of 12; zero non-symlink unreachables). walkLeafFiles applies entry.isFile() after entry.isDirectory(), and Dirent.isFile() is false for a symlink, so the walk neither recurses nor emits. The CI freshness gate regenerates with this same walker, so it byte-compares green over the incomplete set.
findingDetails.impact: The hub documents a per-surface implement-debug-verify doctrine, links it into each surface, and then fails to type it; a reader resolving behaviour through leaf-manifest.json cannot see the doctrine the hub prose says the surface carries.
findingDetails.recommendation: Make the walker resolve symlinks (use fs.statSync or follow the link) or copy the doctrine into each surface instead of linking it. No fix was made during this review.
findingDetails.scopeProof: Enumerated every file under all 17 packets' references/ and assets/ and compared against each mode's manifest rather than sampling; traced the mechanism to the generator walker; checked the symlink targets resolve.

findingDetails.title: Implement-debug-verify doctrine reachable only by prose citation in four surfaces
findingDetails.evidence: SKILL.md:39 says the doctrine lives once in shared/references/workflow-*.md and is symlinked into each surface. SKILL.md:62 defines hub-level inputs as control resources that resolve on disk but never project as leaves, and ROUTER.md:629-637 declares eight SHARED_CONTROL_RESOURCES paths, none of which is a workflow-*.md. So the originals are non-leaves by design, the surface copies are symlinks the walker skips, and the files appear in no manifest. All eight declared control resources do resolve on disk, so the carve-out itself is sound.
findingDetails.impact: The doctrine is reachable by prose citation only, which is precisely the surface the manifest exists to formalise, and the hub either/or against its containment rule is unresolved.
findingDetails.recommendation: Add the three workflow doctrine files to SHARED_CONTROL_RESOURCES so their non-leaf status is declared, or type them as leaves. No fix was made during this review.
findingDetails.scopeProof: Read the hub containment rule, listed and existence-checked all eight declared control resources, confirmed no workflow file appears among them, then checked shared/references for the originals.

findingDetails.title: Two sk-code surfaces sit at 0.1.* against 1.0.0.2 or above with no changelog explanation
findingDetails.evidence: sk-code-mobile-cli=0.1.11.0 and sk-code-obsidian=0.1.0.0 against sk-code-review=1.6.0.0, sk-code-webflow=1.1.0.0, sk-code-opencode=1.0.0.5 and sk-code-quality=1.0.0.2. Both are registered as live packetKind entries. The gap does not track packet size: quality and review have the smallest leaf counts (3 and 10).
findingDetails.impact: A reader cannot tell whether these two surfaces are current or neglected, and the 0.1.* prefix implies pre-1.0 for two live registered modes.
findingDetails.recommendation: Add a changelog entry explaining the 0.1.* line, or promote both to the sibling major line. No fix was made during this review.
findingDetails.scopeProof: Read all six sk-code mode SKILL.md version fields and the hub changelog entries, then checked whether the low versions tracked packet size, which they do not.

reviewDepthApplicability.reason: Seventeen mode packets across three hubs, 474 leaf files, a generator-produced manifest, and mode-level version fields compared against sibling surfaces.

targetSelection.selectionReason: Reachability is decided by the manifest generator, so the walker plus the four surfaces that use symlinks are the highest-value targets for the property the angle names second.

searchActions.result: 12 unreachable files, all symlinks, across four sk-code surfaces; zero everywhere else in the fleet.

searchLedger.hypothesis: The generator walker emits symlinked files.

searchActions.queryOrPath: read walkLeafFiles and test Dirent.isFile against the symlink entries
searchActions.result: entry.isDirectory() then entry.isFile() means a symlink satisfies neither, so it is neither recursed nor emitted.

searchLedger.rationale: Mechanism-level confirmation of the producer defect behind the surface symptom.

searchLedger.hypothesis: The CI freshness gate would catch an incomplete manifest.

searchActions.queryOrPath: read the gate and confirm it regenerates with the same generator before byte-comparing
searchActions.result: It regenerates with buildManifestBytes from the same module, so it green-lights the set the same walker produced.

searchLedger.rationale: The gap is invisible to the gate that exists to catch manifest drift, which is part of F011's impact.

searchLedger.invariant: Hub-level inputs that never project as leaves are all declared in SHARED_CONTROL_RESOURCES.

searchActions.result: Eight declared, all eight resolve on disk, but no workflow-*.md appears among them while three such files exist in shared/references.

searchLedger.rationale: The carve-out is sound for what it lists; the doctrine files are outside its declared scope while also being non-leaf by design.

searchLedger.hypothesis: Mode version fields are comparable across sibling surfaces.

searchActions.result: Two surfaces at 0.1.* against four at 1.0.0.2 or above, with no changelog explanation and no size correlation.

searchActions.result: system-deep-loop 122 files 0 symlinks; cli-external-orchestration 66 files 0 symlinks; sk-code 286 files 12 symlinks.

searchLedger.ruledOutReason: Zero symlinks in the other two hubs makes the walker's skip behaviour unreachable there.

searchActions.result: No mode-registry entry in any hub carries a per-mode version key, so there is no projection to disagree with.

focus: Angle 4 — feature catalogs against the runtime

findingDetails.title: Compiled-routing catalog cites a superseded runtime layout generation in four places
findingDetails.evidence: The entry and the hub index cite .opencode/bin/lib/compiled-routing/011-runtime-engine/lib/resolve.cjs (live: 014-runtime-engine) and .opencode/bin/lib/compiled-routing/010-live-activation/activation/system-deep-loop/manifest.json (live: 013-live-activation). Neither stale directory exists; the layout root holds 003, 004, 005, 008, 009, 013, 014. The entry prose is written around the stale paths in the present tense. The front door executes correctly today.
findingDetails.impact: The catalog's stated purpose is current-state inventory of the hub surface, and its description claims coverage of the live default-on compiled-routing fast path, while its resolution-order description is written against the wrong generation.
findingDetails.recommendation: Update the four reference sites to 013-live-activation and 014-runtime-engine. No fix was made during this review.
findingDetails.scopeProof: Listed the live layout root, resolved both current paths, executed the front door to prove runtime correctness, and read compiled-route-layout.cjs for the generation-mixing contract.

findingDetails.title: Eight catalog entries cite files absent at the cited path across four verified stale-reference classes
findingDetails.evidence: (a) Two archived-track spec paths (.opencode/specs/deep-loops/031-... renamed to 025- and moved to specs/system-deep-loop/z_archive/); (b) a coverage-graph MCP handler at system-spec-kit/runtime/handlers/coverage-graph/convergence.ts where that directory does not exist and no such basename exists repo-wide; (c) two playbook path pairs using the old numeric-prefixed filenames 029_insight_status_prevents_false_stuck.md and 027_resource_map_emission.md against the renamed kebab-case files; (d) two citations of system-spec-kit/runtime/scripts/tests/resource-map-extractor.vitest.ts against the live runtime/tests/ location. Plus validation/system-deep-loop-guard.md at :86, a feature-file path naming no file in its own directory.
findingDetails.impact: Every one of these is a dead pointer for a reader following the catalog, whose contract is that entries name live files or functions.
findingDetails.recommendation: Repoint the nine references to their live paths, or mark the two archived spec paths as historical provenance. No fix was made during this review.
findingDetails.scopeProof: Resolved all 445 references against four candidate roots plus a repo-wide basename index, then hand-verified each surviving miss against the live tree.

findingDetails.title: Runtime catalog prose claims 55 entries while four independent counts all give 54
findingDetails.evidence: Prose says 55 entries. The per-category coverage table sums to 54 (4+1+3+13+2+6+5+5+8+2+3+2), the index carries 54 level-3 entry headings, 54 index links resolve to entry docs, and 54 entry docs exist on disk excluding the index.
findingDetails.impact: A reader checking catalog completeness against the headline number finds a one-entry shortfall that does not exist; the index itself is structurally sound with no missing or orphaned links.
findingDetails.recommendation: Correct the sentence to 54. No fix was made during this review.
findingDetails.scopeProof: Counted four independent ways rather than trusting one, and confirmed the consolidation paragraph's shared contracts are explicitly outside the numbered entries.

findingDetails.title: Catalogs name three of the runtime's seven cli executor kinds, omitting cli-hermes, cli-codex and cli-pi
findingDetails.evidence: executor-config.ts:11 exports EXECUTOR_KINDS with native plus seven cli-* kinds. Across the hub and runtime catalogs the only cli-* tokens present are cli-claude-code, cli-opencode, and cli-surface, which is not an executor kind. Six of seven CLI kinds are unnamed, including the newest and the two fan-out paths use most.
findingDetails.impact: An inventory of the runtime surface that never names most executor kinds its own executor feature supports is thinner than its coverage table implies.
findingDetails.recommendation: Enumerate supported kinds in the executor-config catalog entry, or narrow the coverage claim. No fix was made during this review.

focus: Angle 5 — playbooks and READMEs against the runtime

findingDetails.title: Compiled-contracts README headline count is wrong and the same error appears twice more in the legacy README
findingDetails.evidence: compiled/README.md:19 says the directory 'stores the four flattened command contracts'; it stores three (deep-ai-council, deep-research, deep-review). The same document at :23 says the inventory 'is intentionally limited to the three commands registered with the contract compiler and renderer', and its own tree block at :29-36 lists three contracts plus manifest.jsonl and README.md. Object.keys(require(compile-command-contracts.cjs).COMMANDS) returns exactly three keys. legacy/README.md repeats the error at :13 ('the four compiler-managed deep commands') and :87 ('exactly these four body-to-contract pairings'), while :19 of that file says the directory 'stores three fallback command bodies' and its tree at :29-35 lists three.
findingDetails.impact: The wrong number is the first sentence a reader meets in the document the angle names as its highest-value target, and it is self-refuting within the same file, so a reader has no way to tell which statement is authoritative.
findingDetails.recommendation: Change 'four' to 'three' at compiled/README.md:19, legacy/README.md:13 and legacy/README.md:87. No fix was made during this review.
findingDetails.scopeProof: Listed both directories, read the compiler's COMMANDS registry directly rather than inferring the roster, and compared each count sentence against the tree block in its own document.

findingDetails.title: Deep-review playbook asserts no automated test suite exists while 18 deep-review test files do, and attaches no test cross-reference
findingDetails.evidence: Line 610 reads 'No dedicated automated test suite currently exists for deep-review.' and the section then names documentation paths only. Eighteen test files carry the name or the reducer contract: eleven under system-deep-loop/runtime/tests/ (deep-review-reducers, deep-review-state-reducer, deep-review-state-contract, deep-review-deltas-contract, deep-review-ledger-schema, deep-review-projections-contract, deep-review-sealed-artifacts, deep-review-strategy-heading, review-depth-validator, review-depth-graph, review-depth-convergence), one under system-spec-kit/runtime/tests/deep-loop/review-depth-reducer, and six under system-spec-kit/runtime/cli/tests/ (deep-review-auto-restart-contract, deep-review-contract-parity, deep-review-reducer-schema, review-record-validation, review-reducer-fail-closed, review-research-paths). The packet also ships deep-review/scripts/tests/reduce-state-summary-fallback.test.cjs, documented in its own scripts/tests/README.md.
findingDetails.impact: A false negative terminates the search rather than merely omitting it, so an operator reading the section stops looking at a live 18-file suite. The two sibling playbooks that carry the section show the intended form: deep-research §15 names two spec-kit test files and deep-ai-council §16 maps nine test files to scenario IDs.
findingDetails.recommendation: Replace the assertion with a test cross-reference in the sibling form, at minimum naming the eleven runtime/tests files and the packet's own reduce-state-summary-fallback.test.cjs. No fix was made during this review.
findingDetails.scopeProof: Enumerated every test file matching the packet name or its reducer contract across the tree, then executed the packet's own test to confirm it is live, then read both sibling playbooks to establish the intended section form rather than assuming one.

findingDetails.title: Legacy README presents a repository-wide command-reference checker as a local acceptance test with a guaranteed pass
findingDetails.evidence: Line 108 instructs running node .opencode/commands/scripts/validate-command-references.cjs with the expected result at :111, 'the checker reports that command references resolve cleanly'. Executed, it exits 1 and prints 'FAIL  10 unresolved command reference(s)', listing ten missing assets under .opencode/skills/sk-design/. None of the ten belongs to a deep-loop tree and the README's own subject resolves cleanly inside that run.
findingDetails.impact: Bounded: the document's subject is unaffected, but its stated expected result is unconditional while the command's scope is repository-wide, so the instruction cannot pass for any reason connected to this README.
findingDetails.recommendation: Scope the check to the deep-command trees, or state the known-failing surface explicitly. No fix was made during this review.
findingDetails.confidence: high on the fact, medium on the causal reading
findingDetails.scopeProof: Executed the cited command, read its exit status and full failure list, and confirmed none of the ten failures falls in the document's subject tree before filing rather than treating the non-zero exit alone as the defect.

results.summary: The phase spec names no resolution authority for the four routing-parity properties it requires, and four of five disagree for the system-deep-loop hub. No hard gate failure: the target is a review packet whose spec scopes the finding set rather than asserting a shipped contract.
The phase spec carries no per-iteration checklist rows; its REQ rows are assessed at synthesis.
Four stale-reference classes, one internal count mismatch and one coverage gap confirmed across 445 resolved catalog references; catalog index integrity itself is sound.

Every playbook command and flag resolves, and the deep-review playbook own scenario counts are correct, but its test cross-reference is a false absence claim and two READMEs misstate their own inventories.
